title: Call Centre Advisor
description:
DK Recruitment are seeking a Call Centre Advisor to join a busy customer service team in Plymouth. This is a great opportunity for someone with strong communication skills, a confident telephone manner and good IT skills who enjoys helping customers and working in a fast-paced environment.

Key Responsibilities:
- Handle incoming customer calls.
- Record customer requests accurately and ensure jobs are allocated promptly.
- Monitor and chase outstanding jobs to ensure agreed targets and timescales are met.
- Provide a high level of customer service, keeping customers informed throughout the process.
- Maintain accurate records and ensure data is entered correctly into company systems.
- Follow company procedures and quality standards.
- Identify and escalate issues where further support or approval is required.
- Work closely with colleagues to ensure the smooth running of daily operations.
- Complete general administrative duties as required.

The Ideal Candidate:
- Previous experience in a call centre or customer service role.
- Excellent communication and active listening skills.
- Confident using computers and customer management systems.
- Strong attention to detail and accurate data entry skills.
- Able to work well under pressure and manage multiple tasks.
- A proactive approach, with the ability to use initiative when required.
- A reliable team player with a positive attitude.

title: Customer Service Advisor - Hybrid
description:

title: Resource Management Planner
description:
Adecco are pleased to be recruiting for a Resource Management Planner to work within the Devon & Cornwall Police Force

Location: Plymouth
Contract Type: Temporary
Hourly Rate: 14.10 per hour
End Date: February 2027
Working Pattern: Full Time, Monday to Friday 37 hours per week

Please note this role is subject to POLICE VETTING you must have been residing within the UK for a minimum of 5 years

Are you passionate about resource management and planning? Our client is seeking a dedicated and skilled Resource Planner to join their team in Plymouth. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to operational policing by ensuring optimal staffing levels and responding effectively to the dynamic demands of the organisation.

Key Responsibilities:

As the Resource Planner, you will play a pivotal role in delivering effective resource plans to meet the diverse needs of various business areas. Your main responsibilities will include:
- Maintaining Staffing Levels: Ensure adequate staffing for daily policing activities and planned or spontaneous operations.
- Addressing Shortfalls: Proactively identify and report any staffing shortfalls, escalating issues as necessary.
- Data Management: Accurately record data within the Force IT Systems to enable the creation of comprehensive resource plans.
- First Point of Contact: Provide professional and courteous support for resource management inquiries, handling requests and issues with confidence.
- Skill Base Maintenance: Support the upkeep of the organisational skill base, ensuring staff have the appropriate training and skills.
- Reporting & Analysis: Produce insightful reports to aid managers in making informed resourcing decisions.

Essential Qualifications and Skills:

To thrive in this role, candidates should possess:
- A solid understanding of resource management and planning, along with knowledge of relevant IT systems.
- Familiarity with Working Time Regulations.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, enabling effective interaction with staff at all levels, including senior officers.
- Proficiency in MS Office, especially Excel, Teams, and Outlook.
- The ability to analyse large data sets and quickly identify gaps or inconsistencies.
- Proven experience of working under pressure and meeting tight deadlines.
- Strong negotiation and influencing skills.

Competency Framework:

The ideal candidate will embody the following competencies:
- Emotional awareness
- Ownership and accountability
- Collaboration and teamwork
- Support and inspiration
- Critical analysis
- Innovation and open-mindedness

Why Join Our Client?

This temporary position offers a unique chance to be part of an organisation that plays a vital role in public safety. The successful applicant will benefit from a supportive environment where they can develop their skills and contribute to meaningful outcomes.

If you are looking for a rewarding opportunity to utilise your resource planning expertise, don't miss out!

How to Apply:

Interested candidates are encouraged to apply by submitting their CV and a cover letter detailing their relevant experience. The selection process will focus on identifying individuals who align with the organisational values and can contribute positively to the team.

Become a key player in ensuring that the organisation meets its staffing needs effectively. Apply today and take the next step in your professional journey!

title: Scheduling Co-ordinator Part time
description:
Scheduling Coordinator - Part time

Location: Plymouth
Reports to: Branch Manager
Hours: Part-time, 2-3 days per week (up to 22 hours)
Salary: 26,400 per annum (pro rata)

About Universal Fire & Security

Universal Fire & Security is a trusted provider of fire and security solutions, delivering high-quality installation, maintenance, and support services to customers across the region. As part of the growing Ranger Group, we are proud to be part of a nationwide network of specialist businesses committed to raising industry standards and providing complete peace of mind for our clients.

We are looking for an organised and proactive Scheduling Coordinator to join our team in Plymouth. This is an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys coordinating people, managing schedules, building customer relationships, and contributing to the success of a growing business.

The Role

As Scheduling Coordinator, you will play a key role in ensuring the efficient delivery of installation projects. You will be responsible for managing engineer schedules, coordinating resources, liaising with customers, and supporting the wider installation team to ensure projects are completed smoothly and on time.

This position is ideal for an adaptable individual who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is keen to develop their skills as the business continues to grow.

Key Responsibilities

Scheduling & Coordination
- Manage engineer diaries and schedule installation, pre-installation, and after-care visits.
- Coordinate site visits for engineers and sales personnel.
- Liaise with engineers to support efficient project delivery and workflow planning.
- Maintain project planners and track installation progress.
- Attend installation and planning meetings to support operational efficiency.
- Schedule installation handovers and snagging reviews.

Customer Service & Communication
- Build and maintain strong relationships with customers.
- Keep clients informed throughout the installation process.
- Conduct customer care calls following service visits.
- Handle incoming telephone enquiries and provide administrative support.

Administration & Systems
- Maintain accurate customer records using SIMPRO and FieldMotion.
- Input new customer information into company systems.
- Prepare job packs, installation paperwork, and welcome packs.
- Scan and upload documentation to internal systems.
- Produce quotations for parts and labour and support quotation preparation.
- Compile weekly and monthly operational reports and figures.
- Chase outstanding quotations when required.
- Prepare and collate monthly timesheets.

Resource & Compliance Support

Order equipment and materials for installation projects.

Monitor van stock levels and arrange replenishment where required.

Support training administration, including maintaining training records and assisting apprentice development.

Assist with health and safety administration, including engineer audits, vehicle checks, PPE monitoring, toolbox talks, and compliance documentation.

Support annual audits and wider business compliance activities.

What We're Looking For

Excellent organisational and planning skills.

Strong communication and customer service abilities.

Ability to manage multiple priorities and work effectively in a busy environment.

High attention to detail and accuracy.

Confident using Microsoft Office and business management systems.

Experience in scheduling, coordination, administration, or customer service is desirable.

Experience within the fire, security, construction, engineering, or service industries would be advantageous but is not essential.

Benefits

26,400 per annum (pro rata).

Pension scheme.

Private health insurance.

Life insurance.

Employee Assistance Programme.

25 days annual leave plus bank holidays (pro rata), with the option to purchase additional leave.

Clear opportunities for career progression within the Ranger Group.

Supportive and collaborative team environment.

Equal Opportunities

Universal Fire & Security and the Ranger Group are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive workplace. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, disability, gender, gender identity, marital status, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, or sexual orientation.

Apply today and become part of a growing team where your contribution truly makes a difference.

title: Administrator
description: 12 Month Fixed Term or 12 Month Secondment 37.5 hours per week We are looking for an enthusiastic and organised administrator with good communication and interpersonal skills to join our administrative team within Specialist Nursing Services. Our service supports the delivery of care across the Continence Service, Lower Limb Service, DN Treatment Clinic, Community Tissue Viability Service and Lymphoedema Service. We are seeking a flexible individual who meets the essential criteria outlined in the job description and can provide high-quality administrative support to the team. The successful candidate will work closely with colleagues across the services to support the smooth day-to-day running of administrative processes. You will need to be well organised, able to manage your workload effectively, and capable of working in a busy environment with competing priorities. A positive approach, attention to detail, and a willingness to work as part of a team are essential. Please note that Livewell may close the job advertisement earlier than the specified deadline if a high number of applications are submitted. Therefore, we recommend you submit your application at the earliest opportunity. You will provide a high-quality administrative support service within the Specialist Nursing Service, helping to ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the team and supporting the delivery of a patient-focused service. You will undertake a variety of administrative duties, including reception and telephone responsibilities, maintaining accurate records, data entry, booking appointments, processing correspondence, and supporting meetings through minute taking where required. You will work closely with colleagues to help ensure business priorities are met and administrative processes are completed efficiently and accurately. You will be a first point of contact for patients, carers, healthcare professionals and partner organisations, responding to enquiries in a professional, courteous and confidential manner. You will work proactively as part of a wider team, providing flexible administrative support and contributing to excellent customer service and effective working relationships. You will need to be organised, reliable and able to manage a varied workload whilst maintaining a high standard of accuracy and attention to detail. Please see the job description in the attachments for a complete breakdown of duties. All Livewell Southwest staff are expected to able and willing to work across a 7 day service. Job Share(s) Considered Please note that this role is not eligible for sponsorship under the Skilled Worker route. Dimensions and Context of Role To deliver an effective and competent level of administrative support and consistently deliver a client focussed service which promotes good customer service and effective working relationships. To be responsible for providing daily administrative support in the allocated service area ensuring business priorities are met for example: maintaining records, minute taking, data inputting and reception duties. Working proactively to support team. The job description and person specification are an outline of the tasks, responsibilities and outcomes required of the role. The job holder will need to be flexible to carry out any other duties as may be reasonably required by their line manager. Key Tasks and Responsibilities of the Post Provide support to customer and visitor reception areas, acting as the first point of enquiry and sign posting individual to relevant information / service. Promote the image of the department, checking that notices and leaflets are up to date & well presented. Ensure that all complaints, compliments, concerns, comments and suggestions are appropriately recorded, and where possible resolved within level of role or escalated appropriately. Respond to telephone, email and written queries on behalf of the service area including call handling where appropriate as agreed with line manager. Arrange appointments, meetings and events on behalf of the service, making bookings where necessary and ensuring all equipment and documentation is available, in conjunction with line manager where required. To produce minutes as an accurate record of meetings, transcribing and distributing as directed, with supervision as appropriate. To maintain accurate and timely electronic and hard copy information using organisational systems as directed and in line with policies. Supporting operational staff to access management information; electronic and hard copy. Collect data to enable managers to monitor budgets and performance in relation to business support function with support of line manager. Collect and prepare information for service area users with support of line manager. Maximise the use of electronic systems to enable effective management of the service area such as Microsoft Office and patient record systems. Be compliant with the Data Protection and record management policies and procedures with particular reference to confidentiality and safeguarding issues. Be proactive and contribute ideas for improvement in the way the service is delivered. Able to work on own initiative, prioritising work within defined policies and procedures to set timescales. Ensure that all office support services e.g. post, fax, filing, photo copying, are delivered in a timely manner. Demonstrate own activities to new or less experienced employees. To process and pass for payment all relevant invoices in a timely manner in accordance with business process, with support of line manager To support the line manager with banking and remittance service (including petty cash). Monitor stock e.g. stationery and order supplies and equipment as required within the business area. Undertake research and development as directed. Physical Effort: Frequent sitting & standing. Inputting at a keyboard for most of day, frequent light effort to lift, sort & file case notes. May have to occasionally move presentation equipment and office supplies or clinic consumables. Mental Effort: Frequent concentration is required when inputting into systems, typing documents, making appointments & processing records with a need to ensure accuracy. The work is usually predictable but there may be interruptions from telephone calls, visitors and staff & occasionally imposed deadlines. Emotional Effort: There may be some exposure to service users who may exhibit difficult & challenging behaviours. Working Conditions: Exposure to unpleasant conditions is rare/occasional. May be exposed to verbal aggression from patients. Will use VDU for high proportion of time. The flexible nature of the job may require post holder to move within the team or within the wider organisational setting as required and undertake similar duties. Key Behaviour Competencies: Working together Be straightforward in our dealings with each other and build relationships Listen to others and explain the decisions we have made Recognise and remove barriers to action Create an open and positive learning culture Learn from mistakes & ask others for support where necessary Be aware of ones own behaviour, values, attitudes, strengths and weaknesses. Ability to reflect on ones behaviour and change them. Uphold the values and be proud to be part of the organisation Ensure appearance is professional & name badge visible Act With Integrity Be honest and do what you say you will do Take responsibility and be accountable for your actions Guard and build the organisations reputation Take into account the human and social impact of our work Treat everyone in a friendly, courteous manner; smile & make eye contact Building Success Together Be compassionate and accepting of others. Agree on our goals and see them through Treat each other with dignity and respect Learn from each others experiences Understand and recognise each others contributions of being of equal value Be prepared to challenge the status quo Contribute to the organisations success Stretch the boundaries of personal performance Look for better ways of working to achieve improvements Caring for patients Aim to meet the needs of our patients and partners in care Use initiative to enhance care in innovative and imaginative ways Respect individual cultural differences; challenge bias & prejudice Provide a high quality and safe service for patients Maintain privacy and ensure confidential information is kept safe Question poor practice, process & behaviour Health and Safety at Work and Infection Control: The post holder is required to take reasonable care for his/her own health and safety and that of other persons who may be affected by his/her acts of omissions. The post holder is also required to ensure that all staff under his/her control adheres to relevant statutory regulations, Livewell Southwest policies, department safety procedures, COSHH. The post holder is required to conform to Livewell Southwest policies on Health and Safety, Fire procedures and Confidentiality and to attend any training sessions as required. A copy of the Health and Safety Policy is available from the Healthnet or from the Risk Management Department. The post holder is required to conform to Livewell Southwest policies on HIV/and AIDS. The job description may change as the post develops, but such change will not take place without consultation between the post holder and his/her manager. Livewell Southwest has adopted a NO SMOKING policy for staff which applies to all posts. Details of the policy are available on request and will be included in the statement of main Terms and Conditions of service of staff appoint. Livewell Southwest is determined to eradicate healthcare-acquired infection and puts a great deal of emphasis on the responsibility of all staff to ensure their own personal and others compliance with Infection Control (including Hand Washing) Policies. Risk Management: In accordance with the Risk Management Policy, employees will participate, whenever required, with the risk management process. They will support line managers by attending mandatory and statutory training, completing incident/accident forms for every adverse event or near miss that occurs, report all defects and complaints, and communicate any dangerous situation to individuals potentially at risk. Safeguarding Children and Adults All employees have a duty to safeguard and promote the welfare of children and adults and are required to act in such a way that at all times safeguards their health and wellbeing. Familiarisation with and adherence to national and local safeguarding adults and children policies is an essential requirement upon all employees. Livewell Southwest has specific safeguarding policies and in addition, employees also have a responsibility to practice and work within the multi-agency policy developed by the Safeguarding Adults Board and the Safeguarding Children Board. Staff are also required to participate in related mandatory/statutory training. Infection Control: Livewell Southwest is determined to eradicate healthcare acquired infection and puts a great deal of emphasis on the responsibility of all staff to ensure their own personal and others compliance with Infection Control (including Hand Washing) Policies. All staff must comply with infection control policies and guidance, attend relevant updates and report issues of concern to their immediate line manager (if no action or explanation received, then it is the individuals responsibility to escalate their concerns Sustainability and climate change: All staff are expected to take responsibility for the reduction of carbon emissions within their area of the organisation. In particular this may relate to reducing energy consumption, making low carbon travel choices, consideration of goods and services being purchased, and waste reduction.
